note: A screen, not an audit: questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them. No savings are computed; typical benefits are the cited sources' general wording.

questions.question: Is the compressed air header pressure higher than the end users need?

evidence.text: equipment C-A reads "C-A Fictional AIR COMPRESSOR"
instrument PIC-A reads "PIC-A Supplied pressurecontrol candidate" at C-A

data_requests.item: Header pressure profile and the minimum end-use pressure
where: historian or DCS trend for PIC-A (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
a walkdown: pressure at the farthest and most demanding users
data_requests.how: Find the highest pressure any user truly needs.

questions.decision_rule: Lower the setpoint toward the highest true end-use need plus distribution losses.

typical_benefit.wording: "for every 2 psi decrease in discharge pressure, energy consumption will decrease by approximately 1 percent at full output flow." With 30-50% unregulated usage, "about 1 to 1.6 percent for every 2 psi."
typical_benefit.arc: 2.4231 (IAC/ITAC browse page: 6,522 recommendations, 0.5 yr average payback, 51.6% implemented; average dollar figure omitted)
source_titles: S11: Improving Compressed Air System Performance: A Sourcebook for Industry, 3rd ed. (DOE + Compressed Air Challenge)
S24: DOE IAC/ITAC database: browse pages, download, schema document

questions.limits: IAC/ITAC figures are browse-page averages read through a summarizing fetch and not re-verified against the downloadable database; averages are skewed by outliers.
